Local symbols (flagged to the editor): $r_\pm = x_{1,i\pm1/2}$ and $\theta_\pm = x_{2,j\pm1/2}$, the faces of one cell;
$f^{(a)}_{i\pm1/2}$ the $x_1$ face flux of the momentum component $m_a$ (`flux1[IVY]`, `flux1[IVZ]`) [kg m$^{-1}$
s$^{-2}$]; $p_{i\pm1/2}$ the face pressure returned by the Riemann solver [Pa].

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: the exact $r^2\sin\theta$ measures of a spherical-polar cell, volume centroids for the cell centres, and the
curvature source terms of the momentum equations. **Switch**: YAML `geometry.type: spherical-polar`. **Default**:
off. **Requires**: $x_2$ inside $[0,\pi]$. **Order**: the metric is exact; the source terms are second order.
**Defining equation**: @eq-ch03-sphpolar-metric.
:::

On a spherical-polar grid $(x_1, x_2, x_3) = (r, \theta, \varphi)$ every face area and volume is the exact integral of
the metric over the cell, so the discrete divergence of a uniform field is exact, and the cell centres are volume
centroids, so a stored cell value sits where a cell average of a linear field equals the point value. Because the
basis vectors turn from cell to cell, the momentum equations carry geometric source terms. The radial one can be
written so that the pressure force reduces to the plain face difference of the Riemann solver's face pressure,
which the well-balanced reconstruction of chapter 5 balances against gravity.

The scheme is on when `geometry.type` is `spherical-polar`. Its $x_1$ pressure source has a second form under
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` (chapter 5 owns that form); the curved-face corrections of chapter 4 read the radial face
moments of @sec-ch03-facemoments. The coefficient names `coord_src1_i` to `coord_src3_j` follow the code.

### Derivation

The volume element is $\mathrm{d}V = r^2\sin\theta\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta\,\mathrm{d}\varphi$. Integrating it,
and the area elements of the three face families, over cell $(i,j,k)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{i\pm1/2} &= r_\pm^2\,\lvert\cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+\rvert\,\Delta\varphi, \\
A_{j\pm1/2} &= \tfrac12\left(r_+^2 - r_-^2\right)\lvert\sin\theta_\pm\rvert\,\Delta\varphi, \\
A_{k\pm1/2} &= \tfrac12\left(r_+^2 - r_-^2\right)\Delta\theta, \\
V_i &= \tfrac13\left(r_+^3 - r_-^3\right)\lvert\cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+\rvert\,\Delta\varphi.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-sphpolar-metric}

In the notation of NOTATION.md, $V_i = \varpi_{jk}V^{(1)}_i$ with $V^{(1)}_i = \tfrac13(r_+^3-r_-^3)$ and the solid
angle $\varpi_{jk} = \lvert\cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+\rvert\Delta\varphi$. @eq-ch03-sphpolar-metric is
`face_area1` to `face_area3` and `cell_volume` ([`spherical_polar.cpp:178-211`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L178-L211)).

The cell centres are the centroids of the measure along each axis:

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_{1,i} &= \frac{\int r^3\,\mathrm{d}r}{\int r^2\,\mathrm{d}r}
         = \frac34\,\frac{r_+^4 - r_-^4}{r_+^3 - r_-^3}, \\
x_{2,j} &= \frac{\int \theta\sin\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta}{\int\sin\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta}
         = \frac{(\sin\theta_+ - \theta_+\cos\theta_+) - (\sin\theta_- - \theta_-\cos\theta_-)}{\cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-sphpolar-centroids}

with the integrals over the cell's own interval and $x_{3,k}$ the midpoint. @eq-ch03-sphpolar-centroids is
`radial_centers` and `polar_centers` ([`spherical_polar.cpp:17-28`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L17-L28)); with a single $x_2$ cell the code sets `x2v`
to the midpoint instead ([`spherical_polar.cpp:64-70`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L64-L70)).

The momentum equations in conservation form, written for the physical components $m_a = \rho v_a$, are the divergence
of the momentum flux $\rho\mathbf v\mathbf v + p\mathsf I$ plus terms from the turning of the basis. For the radial
component the extra terms are $\left[\rho(v_2^2 + v_3^2) + 2p\right]/r$. Averaging over the cell, and using that the
measure separates, the factor $1/r$ becomes its volume average and the factor $\cot\theta$ of the $\theta$ equation
becomes its own:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle r^{-1}\rangle_{V_i} &= \frac{\tfrac12\left(r_+^2 - r_-^2\right)}{\tfrac13\left(r_+^3 - r_-^3\right)}, \\
\langle\cot\theta\rangle_{V_i} &= \frac{\sin\theta_+ - \sin\theta_-}{\cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These are `coord_src1_i` and `coord_src1_j` (`coord_src3_j` is the same value). Without face pressures the radial
source is, to second order,

$$
S^{(1)}_i = \langle r^{-1}\rangle_{V_i}\left[\rho_i\left(v_{2,i}^2 + v_{3,i}^2\right) + 2p_i\right],
$$ {#eq-ch03-sphpolar-src1}

computed in `forward` as `src1` ([`spherical_polar.cpp:243-279`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L243-L279)), which is subtracted from the divergence
row of $m_1$. The approximation is the replacement of the cell average of a product by the product of cell values,
an $O(h^2)$ error.

When the Riemann solver returns the face pressures $p_{i\pm1/2}$ and they are inside the $m_1$ flux, the code
replaces $2p_i\langle r^{-1}\rangle_{V_i}$ by

$$
S^{p}_i = \frac{A_{i+1/2}\,p_{i+1/2} - A_{i-1/2}\,p_{i-1/2}}{V_i} - \frac{p_{i+1/2} - p_{i-1/2}}{h_i}.
$$ {#eq-ch03-sphpolar-facep}

@eq-ch03-sphpolar-facep is the `pressure_gradient` branch ([`spherical_polar.cpp:265-275`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L265-L275)). Its
first term cancels the pressure part of the flux divergence exactly, so the net pressure force on $m_1$ is
$-(p_{i+1/2} - p_{i-1/2})/h_i$, the plain face difference. For a uniform $p$ it equals $p\,(A_{i+1/2} -
A_{i-1/2})/V_i = 2p\,\langle r^{-1}\rangle_{V_i}$ by @eq-ch03-sphpolar-metric, so it agrees with
@eq-ch03-sphpolar-src1 in that limit. Under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` the face difference is replaced by `x1_pressure_source`,
the $r^2$-weighted moment of a quintic through six faces ([`spherical_polar.cpp:246-264`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L246-L264)); chapter 5 derives it.

For $m_2$ the source has a curvature part $\langle r^{-1}\rangle\langle\cot\theta\rangle(\rho v_3^2 + p)$, applied
as written, and a part $-\rho v_1v_2/r$ that the code puts in angular-momentum form. Combined with the $x_1$ flux
divergence of $m_2$, the target form is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{A_{i+1/2}f^{(2)}_{i+1/2} - A_{i-1/2}f^{(2)}_{i-1/2}}{V_i}
+ c_i\left(A_{i-1/2}f^{(2)}_{i-1/2} + A_{i+1/2}f^{(2)}_{i+1/2}\right) \\
&\qquad = \frac{r_+A_{i+1/2}f^{(2)}_{i+1/2} - r_-A_{i-1/2}f^{(2)}_{i-1/2}}{x^{\mathrm{m}}_{1,i}\,V_i},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-sphpolar-angmom}

with $c_i = h_i/[(r_- + r_+)V_i]$. The identity follows from $1 \pm h_i/(r_-+r_+) = 2r_\pm/(r_-+r_+)$. The right side
is a difference of face quantities divided by $x^{\mathrm{m}}_{1,i}V_i$, so $\sum_i x^{\mathrm{m}}_{1,i}V_i m_{2,i}$
changes only through the domain-end faces: the $x_1$ fluxes conserve this discrete angular momentum. The same form is
used for $m_3$, and for $m_3$ along $x_2$ with $\sin\theta$ in place of $r$. The code coefficient is `coord_src2_i`
([`spherical_polar.cpp:92-94`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L92-L94)), and the term is added to the $m_2$ and $m_3$ rows through `face_area1`
([`spherical_polar.cpp:281-307`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L281-L307)); the Limits layer records how the code's area factor
differs from @eq-ch03-sphpolar-angmom.

What is exact: the measures, the centroids, the coefficient averages and the telescoping identity. What is truncated:
the product averages in @eq-ch03-sphpolar-src1, at $O(h^2)$. The coefficient averages, the centroid and the two source identities are checked as lines `[C4]` and `[C5]`
of `src/snapy_report/ch03/geometry_check.out`; the tests cited below check the measures, the centroids, the
coefficients and the face-pressure form in the code.

### Numerical method

`x1v` and `x2v` hold the centroids of @eq-ch03-sphpolar-centroids, `x3v` the midpoint; the widths `dx1f`, `dx2f`,
`dx3f` are face differences of the sliced faces, ghosts included, and `dx1v`, `dx2v`, `dx3v` centroid spacings. The
transverse lengths used by diffusion and the curl, `center_width2` $= r\,\Delta\theta$ and `center_width3`
$= r\sin\theta\,\Delta\varphi$, are taken at the centroids. All are built once in `reset`; a mesh generator triggers a
rebuild from the moved faces. The sources run in every stage, in `forward`, after the flux divergence and before the
stage update, and only on interior cells for the face-flux terms; the point-value terms use the primitives of the
whole block. @fig-ch03-sphpolar-centroids shows where the three radial positions of a cell lie.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-sphpolar-centroids
#| fig-cap: "A spherical-polar shell cell between $r_-$ and $r_+$ with its midpoint $x^{\\mathrm{m}}_{1,i}$, its volume centroid $x_{1,i}$ (where the cell value is stored) and the face-measure centroid of its $x_2$ and $x_3$ faces. The arrow marks the outward radial source."
#| fig-alt: "A wedge-shaped shell cell with three radial tick marks, for the midpoint, the volume centroid and the face centroid."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.fig_sphpolar_centroids import make_fig
make_fig()
```

With one $x_2$ cell (`nx2` = 1) there is no $x_2$ flux; the $m_3$ source then uses the point form
$\langle r^{-1}\rangle\langle\cot\theta\rangle\rho v_3v_2$ instead of the $x_2$ angular-momentum form. The
shallow-water equation of state drops the pressure terms from the $m_1$ and $m_2$ sources. The face pressures
`_face_pressure1` exist whenever a block has more than one $x_1$ cell ([`hydro.cpp:160-168`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L160-L168)), so in a hydro
run the face-pressure form @eq-ch03-sphpolar-facep is the one that runs and @eq-ch03-sphpolar-src1 keeps its
pressure term only on blocks with a single $x_1$ cell.

: Code map of the spherical-polar metric. {#tbl-ch03-sphpolar-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-sphpolar-code):

1. `reset` refuses an $x_2$ range outside $[0,\pi]$ with "Spherical-polar coordinates require x2 in [0, pi]" when
   there is more than one $x_2$ cell ([`spherical_polar.cpp:42-48`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L42-L48)).
2. It zeroes the cosine buffers and builds the widths and, with `radial_centers`, the centroids
   ([`spherical_polar.cpp:52-76`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L52-L76)), then the five coefficients `coord_src1_i` to `coord_src3_j`
   ([`spherical_polar.cpp:78-104`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L78-L104)).
3. In each stage `forward` calls the base divergence, then forms `src1` with one of three pressure forms: the quintic
   moment when `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` is set and its stencil is usable, the face-pressure form when face pressures
   are given, else $2p\langle r^{-1}\rangle$ ([`spherical_polar.cpp:243-279`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L243-L279)).
4. It adds the $m_2$ curvature term and the $x_1$ angular-momentum terms of $m_2$ and $m_3$, then the $x_2$
   angular-momentum term of $m_3$ or, with one $x_2$ cell, its point form, as `use_x2_fluxes` selects
   ([`spherical_polar.cpp:281-307`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L281-L307)).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_coordinate` | centroids, areas, volume and the five coefficients equal reference formulas | $10^{-12}$ rel. and abs. | round-off of the closed forms |
| `test_coordinate` | with face pressures the $m_1$ row ignores the cell pressure | $10^{-6}$ rel. and abs. | set in the test |
| `test_coordinate` | the $m_1$ row is the plain face-pressure difference | $10^{-6}$ rel. and abs. | set in the test |
| `test_x1_centroid_rest_python` | a column at rest stays at rest under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` | `TOL_ON` $10^{-10}$ | chapter 5 |

: Tests of the spherical-polar metric. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-sphpolar-tests}

The reference-formula case is `geometry_matches_athena_reference_formulas`
([`test_coordinate.cpp:146-221`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_coordinate.cpp#L146-L221)); it compares `x1v`, `x2v`, the three areas, the volume and `coord_src1_i` to
`coord_src3_j` with `torch::allclose`. The face-pressure cases are
`spherical_polar_radial_source_preserves_face_pressure_gradient` and
`spherical_polar_radial_source_uses_face_pressure_in_x1_momentum` ([`test_coordinate.cpp:645-719`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_coordinate.cpp#L645-L719)); the first
sets the face pressure to the face radius and checks that the $m_1$ row equals
$(p_{i+1/2}-p_{i-1/2})/h_i$, the second checks that two cell pressures give the same $m_1$ row once face pressures
are given. The face-pressure cases run on CPU and, through the `DeviceTest` parameter, on CUDA when it is built; the
reference-formula case runs on CPU only. All are one block, one rank. No case checks the $m_2$ and $m_3$ source
terms. Their pass status at the pin was not run for this chapter (missing evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The $m_2$ and $m_3$ angular-momentum terms are untested: no test at the pin checks them (read from the tests).
- `nx2` = 1 uses a midpoint for `x2v`, not the polar centroid.
:::

A hypothesis from reading the code, not measured: the angular-momentum terms of `forward` multiply `coord_src2_i`,
which divides by the radial factor $V^{(1)}_i$ only, by the full face area `face_area1` $= r_\pm^2\varpi_{jk}$
([`spherical_polar.cpp:286-296`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L286-L296)). @eq-ch03-sphpolar-angmom needs $r_\pm^2$ there, so as
written the term carries an extra factor of the cell's solid angle $\varpi_{jk}$. The $x_2$ term multiplies
`coord_src1_i` and `coord_src2_j` by the full `face_area2` $= \tfrac12(r_+^2-r_-^2)\lvert\sin\theta_\pm\rvert
\Delta\varphi$ where the $\sin\theta$ form needs $\lvert\sin\theta_\pm\rvert$ alone
([`spherical_polar.cpp:297-303`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L297-L303)). If this reading is right, the $-\rho v_1v_2/r$ and
$-\rho v_1v_3/r$ terms are scaled by $\varpi_{jk}$ and the $x_2$ term by a dimensional factor, in every
multidimensional spherical-polar run with tangential velocity; a radial column with $v_2 = v_3 = 0$ does not see it.
This needs a failing test before any change (the editor tracks it as an open question).

The `x2` refusal is skipped when there is one $x_2$ cell. The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the
switch coverage matrix of chapter 12.
